div.l: He wold suffre for a quart of wyne
A good felow to haue his concubyne
A twelf monethes and excuse hym atte Fulle
Ful pⁱriuyli eke a fynche couthe he pulle
And if he fonde owher a gode felowe
He wold techen hym to haue noon Awe
In swiche caas of the Erchedeknes curs
But if mannes soule were in his purse
For in his purs he shuld punysshed be
Purs is þe Erchedeknes helle seide he
But wel I wotte he lyhed riȝt in dede
Of cursyng owȝt eche gilty man hym drede
For curs wille sle riȝt as a · soilyng Sauithe
And also war hym of a significauith
In · daunger hadde he at his owne gise
The ȝonge girles of þᵉ diocise
And knew hir consail ⁊and what was al her rede
A · garlond hade he sette vppon his heuede
As grete as it were for an Ale stake
A bokkler hade he made hym of a cake
With hym þer rode a gentel ꝑpardoner
Of Rouncyuaƚƚ his frend ⁊and his comper
Þat streght was comen frōm þe court of Rome
Ful lowde songe he come hider loue to me
This Somynour bar to hym a stif burdoıı̄un
Was neủer trompe of half so grete a · Sown
Þis ꝑpardoner hade her as ȝelow as wax
But smothe it heng as doth a strike of flax
By ounces heng his lokkes that he hadde
And ther with he his shuldernes ouersprade
But thynne it lay by culpons on ⁊and oon
But hode for Iolite wered he noon
For it was trusset vp in his walet
Hym þoughte he roode al of þe newe gette
Discheuele saf his cappe he rode al bare
